Surah 49: Al-Hujurat (Madaniyyah; it has eighteen verses)

﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger⁠—﴾ "Do not put forward" is from qaddama, meaning taqaddama: that is, do not advance in word or deed ﴿before Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning the one who conveys from Him, i.e., without their permission. ﴿And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing﴾ of your speech ﴿Knowing﴾ of your actions.

It was revealed concerning the dispute between Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding the appointment of al-Aqra' ibn Habis or al-Qa'qa' ibn Ma'bad [as a leader]. And it was revealed concerning those who raised their voices in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 2:

﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ when you speak, ﴿and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾ when you confide in him, ﴿lest your deeds be nullified while you perceive not﴾ — i.e., for fear that this would happen through the raising and loudness mentioned. And it was revealed concerning those who would lower their voices in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), such as Abu Bakr and ʿUmar and others, may Allah be pleased with them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God, those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety﴾ (imtahana): tested (akhtabara) ﴿Allah has tested their hearts for righteousness﴾, i.e., so that it may become manifest from them. ﴿For them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾: Paradise. It was revealed concerning a people who came at the time of midday while the Prophet ﷺ was in his house, and they called out to him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 4:

﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the chambers﴾ "The chambers" (ḥujurāt) are the chambers of his wives (ﷺ), plural of ḥujra, which is that portion of land enclosed by a wall or the like. Each of them would call out from behind a chamber, because they did not know in which chamber he was. ﴿Most of them do not understand﴾ "The calling out of the Bedouins" was with harshness and rudeness, ﴿most of them do not understand﴾ regarding what they did: his lofty station and the veneration befitting it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 5:

﴿Had they been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them.﴾ "Annahum" is in the nominative position by way of the inchoative (mubtada'), and it has been said that it is the subject (fa'il) of a verb understood, meaning "endured" (thabata). ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ toward whoever of them repents.

It was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn 'Uqba, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had sent to the Banu al-Mustaliq to collect the zakat. He feared them because of an old enmity (tirah) that had existed between him and them in the Jahiliyyah, so he returned and said that they had withheld the zakat and had intended to kill him. The Prophet (ﷺ) then resolved to campaign against them, but they came denying what he had said about them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 6:

﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a deviator with information, investigate⁠﴾ — the news (khabar); ﴿investigate⁠﴾ its truthfulness from its falsehood; and in another reading, fa-tathabbatu (tathabbut, "to verify and establish"), from ath-thabat (firmness). ﴿Lest you harm a people⁠﴾ — an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), meaning out of fear of that; ﴿out of ignorance⁠﴾ — a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of the subject, meaning ignorant; ﴿and then become, over what you have done⁠﴾ — become, ﴿regretful⁠﴾ — over the error committed against the people. The Prophet (ﷺ), after they had returned to their lands, sent Khalid to them, and he found among them nothing but obedience and goodness, so he informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 7:

﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah﴾ so do not say falsehood, for Allah informs him of the situation ﴿if he obeyed you in much of the matter﴾ that you report to him contrary to the reality, and then its consequence would be applied to that ﴿you would be in distress﴾ you would have sinned, apart from the sin of causing that which is consequently applied ﴿but Allah has endeared to you the faith and made it beautiful﴾ made it good ﴿in your hearts, and made hateful to you disbelief, defiance and disobedience﴾ this is an exception (istidrak) in meaning but not in wording, because the one to whom faith has been made beloved... etc., his description differs from the description of the one previously mentioned ﴿those are the rightly guided﴾ here there is a shift (iltifat) away from address ﴿the rightly guided﴾ those firm upon their religion

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 8:

﴿As a bounty from Allah﴾, a verbal noun (maṣdar) in the accusative, governed by its implied verb, i.e., He bestows it as a bounty; ﴿and a favor﴾ from Him; ﴿and Allah is Knowing﴾ of them; ﴿Wise﴾ in His bestowal upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 9:

﴿And if two groups of the believers fight⦆ — the verse was revealed concerning an incident: the Prophet (ﷺ) rode a donkey and passed by Ibn Ubayy, and the donkey urinated, so Ibn Ubayy covered his nose. Ibn Rawahah said: "By Allah, the urine of his donkey is more fragrant than your musk." Then there was fighting between their two peoples with hands, sandals and palm stalks.

﴿fa-qtatalū⦆ (they fought) is in the plural, taking into account the meaning, since each group (ṭā'ifah) is a body of people. It is also read as iqtatalatā (the dual), in which case it is in the dual.

﴿fa-aṣliḥū baynahumā⦆ (so make peace between them) is in the dual, taking into account the wording.

﴿fa-in baghat⦆ (but if one of them transgresses) means: exceeds its limits,

﴿iḥdāhumā ʿalā al-ukhrā⦆ (against the other), ﴿fa-qātilū allatī tabghī⦆ (then fight the one that transgresses) ﴿ḥattā tafī'⦆ (until it returns) — meaning: returns ﴿ilā amri Allāh⦆ (to the command of Allah), that is, to the truth.

﴿fa-in fā'at⦆ (and if it returns), ﴿fa-aṣliḥū baynahumā bil-ʿadl⦆ (then make peace between them with justice), that is, with equity,

﴿wa-aqsiṭū⦆ (and act justly), meaning: be just.

Indeed, the believers are brothers in religion, so make peace between your two brothers when they dispute. It is also recited as "إخْوَتكُمْ" (ikhwatikum) with the taa' with a dot above it (bil-fawqaniyya), which makes the word plural "your brothers" in the sense of all of you.

O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people. The verse was revealed concerning the delegation of Tamim, when they mocked the poor Muslims such as Ammar and Suhayb. Mockery (*al-sukhriyya*) means contempt and belittling.

*Qawm* means men among you. "Let not a people [ridicule] a people who may be better than them" in the sight of Allah. Nor [let] women [ridicule] women, who may be better than them. "Do not defame one another," meaning do not find fault, lest you be found at fault; that is, let none of you find fault with another. "Do not call one another by nicknames," meaning let none of you call another by a title he dislikes, such as "O sinner" or "O disbeliever."

"Wretched is the name," meaning the aforementioned mockery, defaming and nicknaming. "Defiance after faith" is a *badal* (substitution in apposition) for "the name," [meaning] that it is defiance, because it has become a habitual repetition. "And whoever does not repent" from that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 12:

﴿O you who have believed, avoid much [of] suspicion; indeed, some suspicion is sin﴾: i.e., sinful. It is much, such as thinking ill of the righteous among the believers, whereas it is rare to think ill of their wicked ones, so there is no sin in it, as in what appears openly from them. ﴿And do not spy﴾: one of the two tā's has been elided from the original, لا تَتَجَسَّسُوا, meaning: do not pursue the faults and defects of the Muslims by searching for them. ﴿And do not backbite (yaghtab) one another﴾: he should not mention his brother with anything he dislikes, even if it is true of him. ﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾ The word مَيْتًا is read with the lightened form (مَيْتًا) and with the doubled form (مَيِّتًا); it means: it is not good for him. ﴿You would detest it﴾: i.e., backbiting him during his life is like eating his flesh after his death. The second has been presented to you, so you dislike it; therefore, dislike the first as well. ﴿And fear Allah﴾: i.e., His punishment for backbiting, by repenting from it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance﴾: He accepts the repentance of those who repent. ﴿Merciful﴾: toward them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 13:

﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾ (i.e., Adam and Eve), ﴿and made you peoples and tribes﴾. Shu'ub (peoples) is the plural of sha'b, with a fatha on the shin, and it is the highest level of lineage. ﴿Qaba'il﴾ (tribes) are below the shu'ub; after them come the 'amā'ir (clans), then the butun (sub-clans), then the afkhadh (thighs), and finally the fasa'il (branches), the last of them. An example: Khuzayma is a sha'b; Kinana is a qabila; Quraysh is an 'imara (the i'rab of its ʿayn is a kasra); Qusayy is a batn; Hashim is a fakhdh; al-'Abbas is a fasila. ﴿That you may know one another﴾: one of the two tā's has been deleted from the original (li-ta'arafu becomes li-ta'arafu with one tā elided), so that some of you may know others, not so that you may boast of the loftiness of lineage. Rather, boasting is by piety. ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing﴾ of you, ﴿Acquainted﴾ with your inner selves.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn** (the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, a concise Qur'anic exegesis):

﴿The Bedouins said﴾: a group from the Banu Asad, ﴿"We believe"﴾: we affirm with our hearts. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted'"﴾: we have submitted outwardly. ﴿And when﴾, meaning: not yet (وَلَمَّا, *lamma*, here equivalent to لَمْ), ﴿faith has entered your hearts﴾ until now, though it is expected of you. ﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ in faith and other matters, ﴿He will not deprive you﴾, read with the hamza and without it, and with the hamza replaced by an alif (يَلِتْكُمْ): He will not diminish you ﴿from your deeds﴾, meaning from their reward, ﴿anything. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ toward the believers, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 15:

﴿Indeed, the believers are﴾ i.e., those who are truthful in their faith, as is made explicit in what follows: ﴿those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, then have not doubted﴾, i.e., have not harboured doubt about the faith, ﴿and have striven with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾. So their striving manifests the truthfulness of their faith. ﴿Those are the truthful﴾ in their faith, not those who say, "We have believed," while nothing of them has been found beyond Islam.

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Do you inform Allah about your religion?﴾ *Mudaʿʿaf* (the doubled, or intensive, form) of عَلِمَ (*ʿalima*, "to know") in the sense of شَعَرَ (*shaʿara*, "to make aware"), i.e., أتُشْعِرُونَهُ (do you make Him aware) of what you are upon in your saying آمَنّا (*āmannā*, "we have believed").

They count it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam, [i.e.,] without fighting, unlike others of them who embraced Islam after fighting against him. ﴿Say: Do not count your Islam a favour to me.﴾ The word مَنصُوب (manṣūb, in the accusative) is governed by the removal of the preposition (nazʻ al-khāfid), namely the بـ (bāʼ, "for"), and the أنْ (an) is to be understood before it in both places. ﴿Rather, God confers a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you are truthful﴾ in your saying, "We have believed."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 49, verse 18:

﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., what is hidden within them. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, with the reading in the yaʾ (they do) and the tāʾ (you do). Nothing of it is hidden from Him.
